title: JIT sandwich of topUp / pullAndRefresh captures disproportionate share of inflow-triggered rate bump
description: Every successful `topUp` or dispatcher-inflow `_syncBudget` performs the reset branch: `windowEnd = now + windowDuration`, `rewardRate = rewardBudget / windowDuration`. If the inflow is large (owner top-up, or a period of accumulated mint-debt being drained), the new rate is strictly higher than the pre-call rate. The reset happens AFTER `_updatePool` settles the pre-call accrual, so the higher rate applies only to time after the reset. An MEV searcher who observes the top-up in the mempool can: (1) front-run with `stake(X)`, (2) let the top-up land, (3) hold briefly to accumulate emission at the bumped rate, (4) back-run with `unstake(X)` and `claim()`. The cost is the NFT units temporarily locked in the contract; because stake/unstake are unrestricted (no lockup), the capital cost is the time-value of the NFTs for one block plus gas.
economicImpact: Searchers extract a slice of every rate-bumping inflow proportional to (searcher's temporary stake / (existing totalStaked + searcher's temporary stake)) × (new_rate - old_rate) × held_duration. Because there is no minimum stake period, held_duration can be one block. With `stakedToken` being the BalancerPooler NFT (non-fungible-ish but ERC1155-transferable), a searcher with access to any amount of the NFT can sandwich every owner top-up.
attackPath:
1. Owner submits `topUp(large_amount)` via public mempool (a routine phUSD refill).
2. Searcher front-runs with `stake(X)` where X is the largest NFT position they can muster. `_syncBudget` runs first, `_updatePool` settles prior accrual, searcher's `user.amount = X`, `user.rewardDebt` snapshots current `accRewardPerShare`.
3. Owner's `topUp` lands. `_updatePool` runs (typically a no-op since it's the same block). `rewardBudget` grows, `rewardRate` jumps up, `windowEnd` resets.
4. Same block or next block, searcher back-runs with `unstake(X)` + `claim()`. `_syncBudget` runs; `_updatePool` accrues at the NEW higher rate over any elapsed time (even one block). Searcher collects the pro-rata share of that accrual.
5. Net searcher profit = X / (totalStaked + X) × (new_rate × elapsed). For a searcher who brings X >> totalStaked, they can capture most of the rate bump's first-block emission.
quantifiedLoss: Per-sandwich loss to legitimate stakers = (X / (totalStaked + X)) × emission_over_searcher_hold_time. With a 540-day window and a 540e18 phUSD top-up raising rewardRate to 1.157e13 wei/sec, one block (12s) of searcher-captured emission at 10x-totalStaked dominance is ~0.9 × 12 × 1.157e13 ≈ 1.25e14 wei ≈ 0.000125 phUSD per sandwich. Small per-event, but repeats on every owner top-up and on every large dispatcher drain. Also the searcher can hold longer than one block for a larger slice (paying NFT time-value).
recommendation: Consider a minimum stake duration or a cooldown between stake and unstake (e.g. ignore rewards for the first N seconds of a stake, returning the forfeit to `rewardBudget`). Alternatively, route owner top-ups through a commit/reveal mechanism or a private mempool submission path. At minimum, document that top-ups are MEV-visible so the owner can prefer private relays. This issue also interacts with the `ownerOrNotGriefed` design: because the modifier explicitly permits rate increases, the sandwich surface is by-design.
affectedParties: Legitimate long-duration stakers whose share of post-topup emission is diluted by sandwichers.
profitability: Modest per sandwich, scales with top-up size and searcher's NFT inventory. Profitable whenever capturable emission exceeds gas + NFT time-value for one block.
